about: Targets of `python -m oh_my_slam.tools.evaluate` (high_level_spec.md §5): metric id -> {op: '<=' or '>=', value}. A metric passes when its value meets the target; it regresses when it is worse than the baseline run by more than max(tolerance_abs, tolerance_rel * |baseline|), using the metric's own tolerances or else the defaults. Edit the values here; no code change is needed.

rationale.about: Why each group of targets has its value. Values under 'measured' are from the run 20260924T230511Z (commit f0a8481, Apple M4 Max 36 GB, warm weights), except for the targets a group below says were set from the baseline run 20260925T022345Z (commit 67b8bc9), and are reference only: the evaluator reads only op, value, the tolerances, unit and description.
rationale.perf.*.wall_s, perf.*.render_s, perf.ser: About 1.5-2x the measured time, rounded: the headroom absorbs run-to-run noise (thermal state, page cache, other load) but not a real slowdown, which the baseline comparison (tolerance_rel 0.2) flags first. Kept where already within ~1.5-2x (reconstruct 3.0 s at 2.1 s, reconstruct -f ply 1.5 s at 0.95 s, mapper one update 300 s at 159 s); tightened elsewhere: cold start 120 -> 45 s (24 s), segment.sh -i 4.0 -> 3.5 s (2.2 s), per frame 2.5 -> 2.0 s (1.07 s), view.sh -i 20 -> 5 s (2.6 s), split mapping 450 -> 360 s (181 s over 3 updates), segment.sh -m 60 -> 2.5 s (1.2 s), view.sh -m 10 -> 4 s (1.9 s). Tightened again to ~1.5x the baseline run 20260925T022345Z (commit 67b8bc9; its values are the 'measured' of these metrics): cold start 45 -> 40 s (24.6 s; the start reads the weights from the page cache, so a little more headroom), segment.sh -i per frame 2.0 -> 1.6 s (1.07 s), one-update mapping 300 -> 270 s (177 s), split mapping 360 -> 300 s (198 s), segment.sh -m 2.5 -> 2.0 s (1.27 s), view.sh -m 4 -> 3 s (1.99 s).
rationale.perf.*.client_peak_mb: About 1.5-1.8x the measured peak resident set of the command's process tree, rounded up: memory is far less noisy than time, so the old 4-12 GB limits (8-18x) could not catch any leak. Single-image commands ~510-535 MB -> 800 MB; reconstruct -f ply 260 MB -> 450 MB; one frame 164 MB -> 300 MB; mapping 4.4-5.0 GB (pycolmap in process + COLMAP children) -> 8 GB; segment.sh -m 1.2 GB -> 2 GB; view.sh -m 462 MB -> 800 MB. Tightened to ~1.5-1.6x the baseline run 20260925T022345Z where the old limit had become loose: one frame 300 -> 250 MB (165 MB), segment.sh -m 2 GB -> 1100 MB (710 MB), view.sh -m 800 -> 350 MB (214 MB since commit af1cda8 serves the map cloud without copying it). Mapping (4.5-4.7 GB, 1.7x) keeps 8 GB: its peak includes COLMAP's children and grows with the sequence.
rationale.perf.server.*, perf.*.server_peak_gb: The server's physical footprint includes its Metal/MPS allocations. Resident after start 9.8 GB -> 13 GB. Single-image commands (and segment.sh -m / view.sh -m, which do not use the server: the figure is its idle footprint) peaked at 10.7-11.4 GB -> 14 GB, i.e. resident plus ~4 GB of activations and caches. Mapping (multi-view inference) 14.7-15.3 GB -> 20 GB, roughly the server's MPS allocation cap (0.7 of Metal's recommended working set on 36 GB); near it the server risks MPS out-of-memory errors.
rationale.pose.*: The references are the commanded headings in the capture names, and the true heading deviates from them: SIFT homographies between the images themselves (pure rotation, measured 2026-09-25) give ~8 deg between 001 and 053 and ~9 deg between 026 and 078, which the names call the same heading, and 004 (commanded +15) at ~15-18 deg. A perfect estimator therefore scores a few degrees of median yaw error and ~9 deg on the same-heading pairs, so yaw_err_median <= 7, yaw_err_max <= 15 and same_heading_yaw_diff_max <= 10 stay: tighter targets would fail a correct map. Registration and pitch direction are exact properties of a working mapper on 79 rendered frames: >= 0.95 (at most 3 of 79 frames unregistered, 1 of 31 tilted frames with the wrong sign), up from 0.9. The head turns in place: the camera circles the neck axis at a few cm, plus the small sideways steps of the bootstrap_side frames, so the camera centres should lie within about 0.1 m; centre_radius <= 0.25 m (was 1 m) leaves room for monocular scale error but rejects the drifting trajectory of the one-update map (0.80 m measured).
rationale.map.*.frame_agreement_*: Spec intent: the map is one consistent cloud. The same-heading pairs see the same surfaces from nearly the same pose, so their stored depths must agree to within monocular depth noise once aligned: median <= 3 % (was 5 %) and p90 <= 10 % (was 15 %), i.e. ~6-9 cm / 20-30 cm at 2-3 m. The one-update map meets this (1.1 % / 6.0 %); the split map (6.8 % / 15.6 %) does not, which is the defect these targets are meant to show.
rationale.map.*.frame_agreement_pairs_*: Spec intent: the map is one consistent cloud wherever keyframes overlap, not only at the two same-heading pairs of §5. Every pair of keyframes whose optical axes are less than 45 deg apart and that share at least 500 pixels is compared, whatever their distance in capture order: sequence neighbours (where keyframe-by-keyframe depth disagrees locally: a scale-only adjustment left keyframes 2 apart at 21 %) and loop closures (where a depth scale that drifted along the sequence shows) alike; the detail reports both subsets (<= 10 and > 10 keyframes apart). Each pair's median disagreement |z_i->j / z_j - 1| measures how differently its two keyframes place the surfaces both see. Targets: the median pair within monocular depth noise, <= 3 % (as for the same-heading pairs); 90 % of the pairs within 5 % (0.1-0.15 m at 2-3 m); at most 1 % of the pairs grossly inconsistent, above 10 % (0.3 m at 3 m: the depth disagreement the near-duplicate test and the object merges tolerate; 1 % leaves room for a few pairs at the edge of the angular range, which overlap only in their image borders where monocular depth is least reliable); and no pair above 15 % (1.5x the gross threshold: a pair disagreeing by 15-20 % draws its shared surfaces twice, 7-10 cm apart at 0.5 m). Measured on maps built 2026-09-25 (one-update / split): keyframe-by-keyframe alignment only (commit 521f1e1): median 1.75 / 1.78 %, p90 7.60 / 7.59 %, above 10 % 6.3 / 6.0 %, worst 20.6 / 21.1 %; one scale per keyframe adjusted over the pairs (commit 385e963): 1.93 / 1.93 %, 5.54 / 5.73 %, 2.7 / 2.7 %, 21.6 / 20.9 % (neighbours alone: worst 20.9 %, 3.5 % above 10 %); a scale and a near/far tilt per keyframe (commit 447f39c, run 20260925T070615Z): 1.78 / 1.81 %, 3.36 / 3.25 %, 0 / 0.13 %, 9.1 / 11.0 % (neighbours alone: worst 9.1 / 11.0 %, 0 / 0.2 % above 10 %; the worst pairs are 42-45 deg apart and overlap only in their image borders).
rationale.map.*.near_duplicates: Spec §2.3: an object observed across several frames keeps one id, so no physical object may be exported twice. Counted: pairs of exported objects with compatible labels that no keyframe observed together (a keyframe that detected both saw two things) whose boxes overlap or lie within 0.3 m. A copy made by inconsistent monocular depth lies along the same viewing rays, offset by the depth disagreement of the keyframes that saw each copy; the frame-agreement target allows a p90 of 10 %, i.e. 0.3 m at 3 m, the distance of the farthest objects of the sequence. Target 0 (the baseline run had 1 in each map: the sink's faucet mapped twice where the 360-degree loop closes). Pairs of horizontal-surface labels (desk, table, counter, kitchen island, bed, rug, carpet, ...) are counted too when their box tops lie within 0.3 m of each other, whatever their label groups: the detector names pieces of one counter top differently (the kitchen island was a desk and, 0.25 m away, a 'rug' at its corner: 1 pair in each map at commit 521f1e1, which the compatible-label rule missed); a rug on the floor under a table is 0.4 m or more below the table top and is not counted.
rationale.map.stability.*: Spec intent: mapping the same sequence in one update or split across several gives the same objects, ids, labels and OBBs. Targets are set at that intent, not at the current values: >= 90 % of the objects paired (was 70 %), >= 95 % of the pairs with a compatible label (was 90 %), >= 80 % with the same id (was 50 %; ids follow the order of first observation, which splitting does not change), median centre shift <= 0.10 m (was 0.15), median size change <= 20 % (was 25 %) and median 3D IoU >= 0.5 (was 0.4; 0.5 is the usual threshold for 'the same box' in 3D detection). label_agreement is measured on a label-blind pairing (geometry alone chooses the pairs whose labels it compares); it used to reuse the pairing of ids and boxes, which adds 1.0 (the whole IoU range) for incompatible labels and so made agreement nearly true by construction. Its detail also gives the agreement over that label-aware pairing.
rationale.seg.*: restaurant.jpg gave 115 objects at the default --min-score 0.5: >= 100 (was 10, which could not notice losing 90 % of the detections). 74 of 79 capture frames have detections: >= 0.9 (was 0.8). seg.min_score >= 0.5 is the --min-score contract. The seg.map_consistency metrics (formerly seg.map.recall / precision) compare the map's objects with per-frame detections of the same detector: they measure consistency, not accuracy. A map object pairs with a per-frame detection under its label or any of its detected_as labels (the labels its detections carried when the detector's label flickered between keyframes and the map merged them). A map object is built from detections in the frames it observes, so map_objects_detected must be ~1 (>= 0.95; measured 0.997); detections_in_map >= 0.8 (measured 0.88) allows the map to drop small or unstable detections. Accuracy is gt.*.
rationale.contract.*: Every contract is a count of violations: 0.
rationale.gt.*: Accuracy against annotations in examples/ground_truth/ (none yet, so never measured). Set from typical monocular performance: object recall >= 0.7, precision >= 0.6, OBB IoU >= 0.3 (monocular boxes of partially visible objects), yaw error median <= 3 deg / max <= 8 deg after the best common offset, pitch error median <= 3 deg. Review them when the first annotations land.
rationale.map.*.mask_out_of_box_share: Spec §2.3/§2.4: an object's box and what the detector saw as the object must coincide. Every detection of an exported object (its mask in the keyframe that detected it, merged ids resolved) is lifted with that keyframe's stored depth and pose; the metric is the largest share, over the objects, of those points outside the object's OBB grown by the depth noise, max(0.05 m, 5 % of the depth). It uses neither the mapper's box fit nor its cloud attribution, only the detector's masks and the stored depth, so mask bleeding onto other surfaces (a 'carpet' mask over a counter and the floor beyond it) or sightings that place the object elsewhere show. Target <= 0.5: most of each object's detected pixels lie on its box; small objects seen at 2-4 m (a teapot, a power outlet) have depth noisier than 5 % and legitimately leave a quarter to a third outside. Measured (one-update / split map): commit 521f1e1 0.51 / 0.51 (teapot, bottle, cup, shelf and paper towel near 0.5), commit 385e963 0.35 / 0.36, commit 447f39c 0.43 / 0.43 — the teapot (a kettle): 4 of its 10 detections (right 040-070, at the image border or 1.3-2.0 m away where the other 6 see it at 2.2-2.5 m) lie 0.4-1 m from its box; the median over the objects fell from 0.013 to 0.003.
rationale.map.*.cloud_out_of_box_share: A check, not a measurement: the mapper attributes a cloud point to an object only inside the object's attribution gate (its OBB grown by max(0.05 m, 3 % of its viewing distance)), for votes and for the fallback that gives an object with too few points the cloud points nearest its own. The metric is the largest share, over the exported objects, of their map-cloud points outside that gate: 0 by construction while the gate holds on every path that labels cloud points (votes, fallback, later updates). Target 0. The independent measurement of box/mask agreement is mask_out_of_box_share.
